o1.biggest_strength: It aims the sequence at the one segment and one moment the pilot actually proves — Controllers at 50–300 people with a live pricing-page change — and its expected-rate logic (6.8% floor, 7.9% ceiling, no multiplying of gains, review at 300 sends) is the honest number the owner asked for.
o1.biggest_mistake: It has no opt-out line or sender postal address, so it is not fully paste-ready cold outreach, and it leaves the non-flagged controllers with only a watch-list mention and no defined next action.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a one-line opt-out and sender address to every email and state plainly what happens to the held contacts whenever their pricing page changes.

o2.biggest_strength: It is the more complete, sendable kit — compliance footer and opt-out, field-fill rules, a hiring-trigger variant, a clean A/B test — with the copy pinned to the persona's own words.
o2.biggest_mistake: It loads all ~1,900 controllers and pushes the unflagged ones with an untested first line, which goes against the owner's read that the pricing-change moment is what works, and its exclusion bullets mix positive-reply rates with meeting rates in a way that can mislead.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the full sequence to contacts with a live pricing-change flag, hold the rest on a watch list, and label every rate in the exclusion list as replies or meetings.

reason: Both would get used, but Output 1 stays on the segment and moment my pilot proves and gives me a reply number I can hold it to; Output 2 is better dressed for compliance yet widens the list against my own data and blurs the rate it is promising.
